newsitem.title: KENYA: DUTCH FREIGHT COMPANY LOSES $50,000 IN KENYAN CARGO.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH FREIGHT COMPANY LOSES $50,000 IN KENYAN CARGO.

text.p: Dutch-owned freight forwarder Flower Wings said on Wednesday it had lost some $50,000 dollars on a cargo shipment of flowers due to the continuing go-slow in Nairobi which is also crippling business at all the country's airports.
As air traffic controllers ended their fifth day of a go-slow by ignoring a government order to resume work losses started to grow and airlines voiced increasing concern for air safety.

"This is really getting bad, we had three chartered flights out of here Monday, all with fresh produce, which all were delayed, one of them for 18 hours," said an official with the Nairobi-based Flower Wings.

He said the three charter flights -- with Martinair, Cargolux and Uganda's DasAir -- all been intended for Amsterdam, with most of the cargo being flowers for the auctions in Holland, which they had now missed. The company normally operates eight charter cargo flights a week.

"The delays are bad for the flowers, bad for the avocados, we are losing money like mad, we had to throw half a load of flowers away, almost ten tonnes -- You are talking about over $50,000 just for that shipment.
"We can't continue like this, if the go-slow continues we will have to cancel our Saturday charter of flowers," the official told Reuters, asking not to be named.
He said Flower Wings, which ships some 1,600 tonnes of air cargo out of Nairobi a month, had also received many complaints from supermarkets in Europe, irritated over the long deliver delays.
"On the vegetable market, supermarkets are already complaining strongly that we cannot deliver on time," he said.

The Horticultural Farmers & Exporters Co Ltd, leading Kenyan brokers in the fresh produce industry,also voiced strong concern over the airport delays at the airport and the risk of losing customers abroad.

"We are very concerned at flights are being cancelled because we will automatically lose. Importers will instead go for other markets where there is no go-slow affecting delivery," said a spokeswoman.

"We are talking about billions of (Kenyan) shillings in losses for the perishable production, as it is a very delicate cargo to transport, and even if some of the farmers can hold back produce now, it will rot if it doesn't get out in time." - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
